decision.rationale: PRR-018 is resolved: readiness completes before dispatch, fd-level framing preserves buffered responses, action no-replay remains intact, real subprocess counterexamples pass, and exact-head CI is green. No open blocking finding remains.

summary: The focused remediation replaces unsafe mixed buffering with an explicit readiness handshake and worker-owned newline framing. Query and action workers each passed 100 immediate-response requests, fresh-worker stress passed at a 0.2-second timeout, and a dispatched unknown action outcome still produced zero fallback calls. PRR-001 through PRR-018 are resolved for the reviewed snapshot.

change_map.change: Use os.read plus a worker-owned byte buffer for newline-delimited UTF-8 frames.

change_map.validation: Coalesced frame, 100 query, 100 action, and fresh-worker stress tests passed.

change_map.validation: Synthetic dispatch marker followed by timeout produced zero fallback calls.

findings.title: Warm worker could lose a buffered response and report a false timeout
findings.observation: The previous select-before-TextIOWrapper.readline loop could leave a complete response in Python's user-space buffer while waiting on an empty kernel fd. The current implementation completes readiness before dispatch and owns all stdout byte framing.
findings.trigger: A newly started worker emits readiness and handles a fast first query or action before the parent consumes readiness.
findings.impact: Queries could falsely time out, and an executed mutating action could be reported as unknown, making manual retry hazardous.

evidence.description: start waits for validated readiness, and response reads consume an owned byte buffer before selecting and reading the fd with os.read.

Real subprocess tests cover coalesced readiness/response frames, failed readiness, 100 immediate query responses, 100 immediate action responses, unknown action timeout without replay, and pipe cleanup.
An exact-head review stress created a fresh worker for every request and passed 100 query plus 100 action first responses at timeout 0.2 seconds.

findings.remediation: Completed: treat readiness as a startup handshake, use fd-level newline framing with an owned buffer, clean process resources, and preserve no replay after action dispatch.
findings.verification: Completed: real subprocess query/action tests, 0.2-second fresh-worker stress, unknown-outcome no-replay, warning-as-error package tests, packaging checks, and exact-head CI passed.

required_actions.action: Repair readiness/response framing, add real subprocess protocol tests, prove fast query/action responses do not falsely time out, and retain no replay after an unknown mutating outcome.

risks.description: Private desktop logs can contain transient UI text.
risks.mitigation: Keep raw artifacts untracked and publish only bounded semantic evidence.

risks.description: A genuine lost mutating-action response can leave the desktop outcome unknown.
risks.mitigation: Never replay after dispatch and require observation or manual recovery.

risks.description: Workers serialize requests and depend on newline-delimited UTF-8 frames.
risks.mitigation: Lock one request to one response, cap frames at 16 MiB, and fail/restart on protocol errors.

risks.description: Startup can wait up to five seconds if framework readiness hangs.
risks.mitigation: Keep startup outside the warm API path and disable the worker on readiness failure.
Public APIs, schemas, configuration, helper behavior, versions, and dependencies remain unchanged.

risks.description: Reverting only this fix restores the known S1 buffering race.
risks.mitigation: Rollback the complete warm-worker slice or disable it; do not restore mixed buffered and fd-level reads.

risks.description: Worker framing and generated scripts remain private details in one large module.
risks.mitigation: Keep focused protocol tests and extract the transport only in a separate cleanup.

limitations: This review is authoritative for head 2f11b23b79040bf315513e1341d15a5e57f72379.
No fresh real desktop mutation was performed after the framing fix.
Historical live evidence proves AppKit worker integration but not delivery read-back or latency percentiles.
Private raw observations and unrelated dirty worktree files were excluded.
The report commit is documentation-only and follows the reviewed snapshot under the repository review-artifact convention.
assumptions: Newline-delimited UTF-8 is the private worker protocol contract.
A mutating request is potentially dispatched once its write and flush are attempted, so subsequent failure must never trigger replay.
Prior live AppKit proof plus direct post-fix subprocess framing proof is sufficient for this transport-only remediation without another desktop mutation.
The 16 MiB private response cap exceeds current bounded selector response limits.
